determinism: No randomness is used. Identical series content and identical SonificationSettings give byte-identical WAV bytes and provenance on the same platform and NumPy build (tested). Across platforms, floating-point libm differences may change isolated PCM samples by at most 1 LSB; two renders are considered equivalent when their provenance (excluding output.sha256) is identical and every PCM sample differs by at most 1 LSB.

engine_mappings.sound_parameter: segment order (which pulse is which sample)
engine_mappings.source_measurement: sample order of the validated series
engine_mappings.rule: The samples are rendered in series order, one segment each, covering the whole duration with no overlap and no gap. Each audible segment is shaped by a linear attack and release envelope, so each sample is one pulse. Every segment records its own timestamp, start_seconds and end_seconds, so the mapping from audio time to data time is always exact.
engine_mappings.rationale: Temporal change is heard as a sequence of pulses that follows the measured time axis.

engine_mappings.source_measurement: rate_normalized in [0, 1], the normalized rate of change derived and documented by the data domain; unused under timing_mode='uniform'
engine_mappings.rule: timing_mode='uniform': every sample gets an equal share of the duration. timing_mode='rate_weighted' (default): a sample's share is proportional to 1 / (1 + rate_sensitivity * rate_normalized), so rapid change gives short segments and a fast pulse, calm stretches give long segments and a slow pulse. The total duration is unchanged; only its distribution moves. Boundaries are computed in exact rational arithmetic. provenance.timing records the mode, the mean and fastest pulse rates, whether the fastest stretch stays below the 20 Hz rhythm floor, and whether the time axis is linear.
engine_mappings.rationale: A uniform pulse makes a long calm stretch and a sudden surge sound equally eventful. Letting the rate of change set the pulse rate means acceleration is heard as acceleration, which is the quantity a listener registers most immediately. The cost is that audio time is no longer proportional to elapsed data time, so linear_time_axis is recorded as false and each segment carries its own timestamp for the exact mapping.

engine_mappings.source_measurement: level_normalized in [0, 1], derived and documented by the data domain
engine_mappings.rule: gain_db = gain_floor_db * (1 - level_normalized); amplitude = peak_amplitude * 10**(gain_db/20). level_normalized = 0 gives gain_floor_db (default -36 dB), 1 gives 0 dB.
engine_mappings.rationale: Perceived loudness grows roughly with the logarithm of amplitude, so equal steps in the normalized level give roughly equal loudness steps. A level of 0 stays audible so that a measured minimum is distinguishable from silence, which means absent data.

engine_mappings.source_measurement: the domain's audibility decision for each sample
engine_mappings.rule: A sample the domain marked inaudible renders digital silence for its whole segment (all PCM samples 0).
engine_mappings.rationale: A gap in the data must not be heard as a measurement, so it is not heard at all.

engine_mappings.source_measurement: pan in [-1, 1], derived and documented by the data domain
engine_mappings.rule: Constant-power law: angle = (pan + 1)/2 * pi/2, left = cos(angle), right = sin(angle), so left**2 + right**2 = 1 at every position. pan = None (unmapped or undefined) is centred. Disabled when pan_enabled is false, which centres every segment.
engine_mappings.rationale: Stereo position is a continuous dimension with no discontinuity, so it carries a second variable without disturbing the loudness that encodes the first.

engine_mappings.rule: Fixed carrier at carrier_frequency_hz with harmonics 1..n at harmonic_amplitudes, normalized by their sum so the waveform peak never exceeds 1 before gain. Phase is continuous across the whole file.
engine_mappings.rationale: No domain maps a measurement to pitch, so pitch must not vary and imply a measurement that does not exist.

domain_mappings.source_measurement: reported COVID-19 deaths or cases for one calendar week, for one location
domain_mappings.rule: level_normalized = log10(count) / log10(reference maximum), with the reference maximum fixed at 1e5 deaths per week (1e8 cases per week). A week of 0 or 1 sits at the gain floor; the single highest week in the global series exceeds 1e5 and clips to 1.0 with flag clipped_high.
domain_mappings.rationale: Weekly counts span five orders of magnitude, so a linear mapping would leave everything except the peak inaudible. A log scale matches how counts are read and reported, and the reference is fixed and cited, so loudness is comparable between locations and never derived from the sample.

domain_mappings.source_measurement: week-over-week ratio of the reported total
domain_mappings.rule: growth_log2 = log2(count / previous week's count); pan = clamp(growth_log2 / 1.0, -1, 1). A doubling pans fully right, a halving fully left, a flat week stays centred. Undefined for the first week and whenever either week is zero or unusable, which is centred and flagged.
domain_mappings.rationale: The magnitude is already carried by loudness, which changes only slowly on a log scale. The rate of change is what a listener experiences as a wave arriving or receding, so giving it its own continuous dimension makes the waves audible rather than merely present.

domain_mappings.source_measurement: magnitude of the week-over-week log2 ratio
domain_mappings.rule: rate_normalized = min(1, |growth_log2| / 2.0), so a quadrupling or a fall to a quarter in one week reaches the fastest pulse and a flat week the slowest. The magnitude only, so a collapsing wave quickens the pulse just as a growing one does. Undefined growth gives an unknown rate, which the engine treats as the slowest.
domain_mappings.rationale: The pandemic's defining feature is acceleration, and a uniform pulse makes a flat month and a doubling week sound equally eventful. Driving the pulse rate from the same growth ratio that drives the pan means a surge is heard as the rhythm quickening while the image moves right. Direction is already carried by the pan, so the rate uses the magnitude and does not duplicate it.

domain_mappings.rule: A week is silent when it has no source rows, when any row in it is null (so the total cannot be known to be complete), or when a value is negative. Every other week sounds, including a reported total of zero.
domain_mappings.rationale: The source posts a week's total on a single weekday and zero on the others, so treating every zero as a measurement would render six silent days a week as six real reports of zero deaths. Absent reporting is rendered as absence of sound instead.

omitted_mappings.rationale: Candidates such as the case-fatality ratio are dominated by testing capacity and reporting practice rather than by the quantity a listener would take them to mean, so nothing is mapped to pitch. Deliberately left for Phase 6 listening validation.

omitted_mappings.rule: Not rendered in the default series.
omitted_mappings.rationale: The default location is World, for which absolute and per-capita series carry the same shape. Per-capita columns exist in the source and are the right choice for comparing countries, which is a later phase.

source.cadence: Weekly: 240 of 1674 rows are non-zero and every one of them falls on a Sunday, so each Sunday row carries that week's total.

selection.reporting_cadence: Weekly: 240 of 1674 rows are non-zero and every one of them falls on a Sunday, so each Sunday row carries that week's total.

mapping_source.level_quantity: weekly reported COVID-19 deaths for World (deaths per week), log10 scaled

level_reference.source: Upper bound: nearest power of ten at or above the global historical peak of weekly reported deaths. WHO Weekly epidemiological update, 19 January 2021, reported a record ~93 000 deaths for the preceding week, and WHO warned of approaching 100 000 deaths per week; the revised Our World In Data / WHO series peaks at 103 719 (week ending 2021-01-24), which clips to 1.0. Lower bound: 1 is the smallest reportable non-zero count, so log10 of the minimum is 0. Accessed 2026-11-14

mapping_source.pan_quantity: week-over-week growth ratio of the weekly total
mapping_source.pan_rule: growth_log2 = log2(count / previous week's count), and pan = clamp(growth_log2 / 1.0, -1, 1), so a doubling pans fully right and a halving fully left. Undefined (null, centred, flagged undefined_growth) for the first week and whenever either week's count is zero or unusable.
mapping_source.rate_quantity: magnitude of the week-over-week growth ratio
mapping_source.rate_rule: rate = min(1, |growth_log2| / 2.0); unknown when growth is undefined
